mainTopic: When ולדי קדשים become holy, a clash between two holy statuses, and whether a fetus counts as part of its mother
overview: The amud opens by asking why, in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling, the offspring of holy animals do not take on their mother's קדושה. The answer is that he holds ולדות קדשים become holy only when they are born. The גמרא then shows from a ברייתא on the פסוק of בכור that another תנא holds they are holy already in the womb. רב עמרם asks what happens when someone declares a בכור an עולה at the very moment it is born. רב ששת compares this to אילפא's question about declaring לקט to be הפקר, and אביי answers that God's word beats a person's word. A new משנה follows about consecrating a mother animal as a שלמים and her offspring as an עולה, where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree. In the גמרא, רבי יוחנן rules that a pregnant animal set aside as a חטאת is like two separate חטאות, because a fetus is not part of its mother. רבי יוחנן is then challenged twice, from the משנה's wording and from a ברייתא about freeing the unborn child of a שפחה. That second challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why don't the offspring get the mother's holiness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling, the offspring are not affected by the קדושה of their mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does holiness not take effect on them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the ruling it just quoted. Why don't the offspring take on the holiness of their mother? This question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We would normally expect a baby animal to share its mother's status, since it is part of her before birth. So the ruling that the offspring are not holy needs a reason. The גמרא is asking for the principle behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes effect on them, rests on them

phrases.english: Why does holiness not take effect on them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the offspring in the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that was just discussed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's earlier ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the offspring do not carry their mother's קדושה.

steps.title: Offspring become holy only at birth
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that ולדות קדשים become holy only when they come into being, meaning at birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the offspring of holy animals become holy only when they come into being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the young of holy animals become holy only from the moment they are born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the holiness starts only at birth, the fetus is not holy while it is inside the mother. That explains why it does not pick up her status while it is still in the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: At their coming into being, at birth

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
the offspring of sacred animals are holy at their coming into being,
phrases.notes: "Coming into being" means being born. Before birth they are not yet holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that ולדות קדשים become holy בהוייתן, only at birth.

steps.title: Proof: otherwise the mother's holiness would already apply
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the reading by showing that the alternative does not work. If offspring were holy in the womb, the mother's קדושה would already have taken hold of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought they are holy from their mother's womb, why would holiness not take effect on them? After all, their mother's holiness has already taken hold of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the answer by testing the other possibility. If the fetus became holy in the womb, it would already be holy with its mother's holiness. Then the ruling that holiness does not apply to it would make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof by elimination. A fetus that becomes holy in the womb is already caught up in the mother's קדושה, so the ruling that no קדושה applies would be impossible. The only reading that fits the ruling is that holiness begins at birth.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it entered your mind (if you were to think)
It has taken hold of them

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that they are holy from their mother's womb,
why does holiness not take effect on them?
But their mother's holiness has taken hold of them!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מִמְּעֵי אִמָּן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 2 by ruling out the alternative.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds holiness begins at birth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic of his own ruling: holiness in the womb would mean the mother's קדושה already applied, which contradicts the ruling.

steps.title: Conclusion: holiness begins at birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, ולדי קדשים are holy only from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the offspring of holy animals are holy only at their coming into being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל must hold that the offspring of holy animals become holy only when they are born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אלא שמע מינה shows that the proof is finished. Since the other option failed, this view is now settled as his opinion. That sets up the contrast with the next תנא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, ולדי קדשים become holy only בהוייתן, at birth, and not in the womb.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
the offspring of sacred animals are holy at their coming into being.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds ולדי קדשים בהוייתן הן קדושים.

steps.title: Another תנא holds they are holy in the womb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that a different תנא disagrees and holds that ולדי קדשים are holy already in the mother's womb. It then sets up a ברייתא to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא holds that the offspring of holy animals are holy from their mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now points to a תנא who disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. This step states his view and sets up the ברייתא that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the opposite view is introduced: holiness begins already in the womb. The proof does not appear yet. It comes at the end of the ברייתא that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: And this tanna holds

phrases.aramaic: וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים מִמְּעֵי אִמָּן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: that the offspring of sacred animals are holy from their mother's womb,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces an opposing view to the conclusion in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A different תנא holds ולדי קדשים ממעי אמן הן קדושים.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a firstborn animal may not be consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "איש אותו" that the פסוק forbids consecrating a בכור animal. It is not forbidding a firstborn person from consecrating things.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: Had the פסוק said only "a firstborn shall not consecrate," I would have said that a firstborn person may not consecrate items. So the פסוק says "a man… it": you may not consecrate it, but a firstborn person may consecrate items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it needs and begins working through the פסוק about a בכור. First it clears up what the word "בכור" refers to in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read alone, "בכור לא יקדיש" could mean that a firstborn person may not make anything holy. The words "איש אותו" show that the בכור is the object being consecrated, not the person doing it. So the ban is on consecrating a firstborn animal, which is already holy as a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn (here, a firstborn animal that is holy from birth)
Had it not been stated (in full)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
Had it been stated only "A firstborn shall not consecrate,"
I would have said
a firstborn person may not consecrate items,
therefore the verse states: "A man… it":
it you may not consecrate,
but a firstborn person may consecrate items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא brought as the source for the תנא in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From "איש אותו": a בכור animal may not be consecrated with another קדושה, but a firstborn person may consecrate things.

steps.title: Maybe only the firstborn person is restricted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a new possibility. Perhaps only a firstborn person may not consecrate the firstborn animal, while others may.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I would still say: he may not consecrate it, but others may consecrate it.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a new doubt is raised. Maybe the ban applies only to the firstborn man himself, and other people would be allowed to consecrate the firstborn animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after step 6, the word "בכור" might still be read as limiting who may not do the consecrating. That reading would leave everyone else free to consecrate the animal. The ברייתא needs another word in the פסוק to rule this out.

phrases.english: But still I would say:
he may not consecrate it,
but others may consecrate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the reading in step 6 is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the ban learned in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban might apply only to a firstborn man, leaving other people free to consecrate a בכור animal.

steps.title: "בבהמה" shows the topic is animals, for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The word "בבהמה" shows that the פסוק deals with firstborn animals, so no one may consecrate them with another קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "among animals": I am dealing with animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the doubt. The word "בבהמה" (among animals) shows that the subject is the firstborn animal, not a firstborn person, so the ban applies to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק is speaking about the firstborn of animals, "בכור" describes the animal. It is not about who may do the consecrating. So no person at all may consecrate a בכור animal for a different קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: I am dealing with, I am discussing

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "among animals":
I am dealing with animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: an extra word in the פסוק fixes its subject.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a firstborn man is forbidden to consecrate a בכור animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: "בבהמה" shows the פסוק deals with animals, so no one may consecrate a בכור animal with another קדושה.

steps.title: A firstborn may be consecrated while still in the womb
steps.stepSummary: From "אשר יבכר לה׳" the ברייתא learns that the ban starts only once the animal is born as a בכור. Before birth, while still in the womb, it may be consecrated with another קדושה. This shows the תנא holds that holiness can take effect in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think one may not consecrate it in the womb either. So the פסוק says "which is born as a firstling to ה׳": once it is born as a firstling to ה׳ you may not consecrate it, but you may consecrate it in the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to teach that a firstborn may be consecrated for another purpose while it is still inside its mother. The ברייתא is not finished yet: steps 10-11 continue it, and the proof the גמרא wants comes in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban applies only once the animal has been born as a בכור. Before birth, while the בכור holiness has not yet taken effect, a new consecration can take effect on the fetus. This sets up the next question: does the same leniency apply to the offspring of other holy animals?

keyTerms.meaning: From when it is born as a firstling

steps.whyThisMatters: This womb leniency for a בכור is the starting point. When the ברייתא refuses to extend it to other ולדי קדשים (step 11), the גמרא shows that this תנא holds they are holy in the womb (step 12).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread this as permitting a second holiness on a בכור. Once it is born a בכור, that is forbidden. The permission is only before birth, while the בכור holiness has not yet taken effect.

phrases.english: One might think he may not consecrate it in the womb either?
Therefore the verse states: "which is born as a firstling to the Lord":
from when it is born as a firstling to the Lord you may not consecrate it,
but you may consecrate it in the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the womb leniency for a בכור, which steps 10-12 build on to prove the view of the תנא in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That this תנא holds ולדי קדשים are holy ממעי אמן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that one may consecrate a firstborn בבטן, showing that holiness can take effect on a fetus.

steps.title: Maybe the offspring of all holy animals can also be given another holiness in the womb
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that the leniency for a בכור in the womb might apply to the offspring of all קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that the offspring of all holy animals are the same, so they too could be given another holiness while still in the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possibility: maybe what is true of a בכור in the womb is also true of the offspring of any holy animal. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 learned that a בכור may be given another קדושה before it is born. The ברייתא now asks whether the same is true for ולדי קדשים, meaning the babies of animals that are already holy. If they were not holy until birth, they would also be open to a different קדושה in the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might think". It brings up a possibility that the ברייתא will then reject.
The offspring of animals that were set aside as קרבנות

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף וַלְדֵי כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים כֵּן,
phrases.english: One might think that even the offspring of all consecrated animals are so,
phrases.notes: "So" means they too could be given a different holiness while still in the womb, just like the בכור in step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף וַלְדֵי כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to extend the womb leniency from step 9 to all ולדי קדשים
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the womb leniency learned in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a בכור can receive another קדושה before birth, perhaps the offspring of any holy animal can too.

steps.title: The word אך separates the בכור from other holy offspring
steps.stepSummary: The word אך limits the leniency to a בכור only.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "אך" ("but"), and this word makes a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the word אך. That word separates the בכור from the offspring of other holy animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words like אך limit a rule. Here it limits the womb leniency to a בכור. The offspring of other קדשים may not be given a different קדושה even while they are in the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches". It brings a word from the פסוק to settle the question.
"But" or "only". A word that limits a rule.
It distinguished, meaning it separated two cases.

phrases.english: The verse states "But". It distinguished,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All ולדי קדשים could get another קדושה in the womb
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a בכור can. Other ולדי קדשים cannot.

steps.title: So this תנא holds that ולדי קדשים are holy in the womb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this ברייתא's תנא holds ולדי קדשים are holy already in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that he holds the offspring of holy animals are holy already in their mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion it was aiming for since step 5. This תנא holds that the babies of holy animals are holy even before they are born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why can't the offspring of other קדשים receive a new קדושה in the womb? Because they are already holy there. A בכור only becomes holy at birth, so before birth it is still free to receive a different קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his opinion

steps.whatToRemember: According to this תנא, ולדי קדשים are holy in the womb. A בכור becomes holy only at birth, so before birth it can be given another קדושה.

phrases.english: Evidently he holds

phrases.aramaic: וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים מִמְּעֵי אִמָּן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁין.
phrases.english: that the offspring of consecrated animals are holy from their mother's womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the reading of אך in step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This תנא holds that ולדי קדשים are holy in the womb.

steps.title: רב עמרם asks: a בכור declared an עולה as most of it comes out
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם asks רב ששת what happens if someone says a בכור becomes an עולה exactly when most of it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said to רב ששת: if someone said about a בכור, "When most of it comes out, it is an עולה", is it an עולה or a בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב עמרם asks about a case where the עולה declaration is set to take effect at the very same moment the בכור holiness takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy when most of it leaves the womb. Here the owner timed the עולה to start at exactly that moment, so neither holiness comes first. The question is which one wins.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering that is burned completely on the מזבח
A firstborn animal. It is holy on its own and goes to the כהן.
The coming out of most of it. This is the moment of birth.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 9. There the other holiness was given while the animal was still in the womb, before it was a בכור. Here the עולה and the בכור arrive at the exact same moment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עַמְרָם לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Amram said to Rav Sheshet:
If one said about the firstborn
"With the coming out of its majority, it is a burnt offering",
is it a burnt offering or is it a firstborn?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עַמְרָם לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a בכור and another קדושה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the עולה and בכור holiness arrive at the same moment, which one takes effect?

steps.title: The two sides: each bit becomes an עולה, or each bit is a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasoning on each side of רב עמרם's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it an עולה, because every little bit that comes out becomes fully burned? Or is it a בכור, because every little bit that comes out stays in its own status as a בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why רב עמרם was unsure. It gives a reason for the עולה side and a reason for the בכור side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the עולה side, each part of the animal becomes an עולה as it comes out, and the עולה is the stronger holiness. On the בכור side, each part that comes out is simply what it naturally is, a בכור. The question is whether the stronger holiness wins or the natural one does.

keyTerms.meaning: Entirely burned. This is the way an עולה is offered.
In its own status, meaning as it naturally is

phrases.english: Is it a burnt offering,
since each and every little bit that comes out
becomes entirely burned,
phrases.notes: Literally "is כליל", meaning it becomes an עולה, which is burned completely.

phrases.english: or is it a firstborn,
since each and every little bit that comes out
is in its own status?

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלָה הָוֵי, דְּכׇל פּוּרְתָּא וּפוּרְתָּא דְּקָא נָפֵיק הָוֵי כָּלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the stronger עולה holiness win, or the natural בכור holiness?

steps.title: Another version of the two sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second way of explaining why רב עמרם was unsure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: is it an עולה, because that holiness takes effect on it? Or perhaps it is a בכור, because its holiness comes from the womb?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the reasons behind רב עמרם's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the עולה side says the owner's declaration of holiness does take hold on the animal. The בכור side says a בכור's holiness comes from the womb, so it is built in from birth. This version stresses that the בכור holiness is natural, not something a person declares.

phrases.english: Another version:
Is it a burnt offering because holiness takes effect upon it,
or perhaps it is a firstborn,
because its holiness is from the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the reasoning given in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the declared עולה holiness take hold, or does the בכור holiness from the womb win?

steps.title: רב ששת links the question to אילפא's question about לקט
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells רב עמרם that his question is the same as אילפא's question about someone who declares לקט to be הפקר at the moment it falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: What exactly is your question? It is the same as what אילפא asked: if a person said about the לקט, 'When most of it falls, let it be הפקר,' is it לקט or is it הפקר?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת does not answer directly. He shows that רב עמרם's question is the same as another known question, the one אילפא asked about לקט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, a holy status from the Torah (בכור, or לקט) and a status a person declares (עולה, or הפקר) try to take effect at the exact same moment. The לקט case gives a clearer picture of the clash: the poor get the grain through לקט, while everyone gets it through הפקר.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest, which the Torah gives to the poor
Ownerless property that anyone, rich or poor, may take
The falling of most of it, the moment the grain becomes לקט

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your question?
phrases.notes: רב ששת is speaking to רב עמרם here.

phrases.english: This is the same as what Ilfa asked:
If someone said about the gleanings
"At the moment most of it falls,
let it be ownerless,"
is it gleanings, or is it ownerless?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ? הַיְינוּ דְּבָעֵי אִילְפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב עמרם's question by comparing it to a parallel question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is the same as אילפא's question about לקט and הפקר

steps.title: The reasoning on each side of Ilfa's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the grain might stay לקט, and why it might become הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it לקט, because its holy status comes from Heaven? Or maybe it is הפקר, because then both poor people and rich people can take it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two sides of אילפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: לקט is a status the Torah itself creates, so it should be stronger. Side two: הפקר lets everyone take the grain, poor people included, so it is the wider status and might win out.

keyTerms.meaning: Its holy status is set by Heaven, not by a person

phrases.english: Is it gleanings,
since its holiness comes from Heaven,
or perhaps it is ownerless,
since both poor and rich can take it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶקֶט הָוֵי, שֶׁכֵּן קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, אוֹ דִלְמָא הֶפְקֵר הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which status wins: the Torah's status of לקט, or the owner's declared status of הפקר

steps.title: אביי: we listen to the Master, not the student
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the question: God's word beats a person's word, so the grain stays לקט, and the same is true for the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What is his question? When the Master's words and the student's words conflict, whose words do we listen to? Here too, whose words do we listen to?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers אילפא's question, and through it רב עמרם's question too. God's command wins over what a person declares.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'Master' is God, who made the grain לקט. The 'student' is the person who tried to make it הפקר. Of course we follow God, so the grain stays לקט. In the same way, the animal stays a בכור and does not become an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of the Master versus the words of the student

steps.whatToRemember: When the Torah's status and a person's declaration take effect at the same moment, the Torah's status wins. So the לקט stays לקט, and the בכור stays a בכור.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: What is his question?
The words of the Master and the words of the student:
phrases.notes: The 'Master' is God, and the 'student' is the person making the declaration.

phrases.english: whose words do we listen to?
So too here: whose words do we listen to?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ? דִּבְרֵי הָרַב וְדִבְרֵי תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question laid out in the previous steps
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God's word beats a person's word, so it stays לקט, and the animal stays a בכור

steps.title: New משנה: consecrating a mother animal and its offspring
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that if someone first makes the offspring an עולה and then the mother a שלמים, both take effect. If he says the mother first, the offspring automatically becomes a שלמים, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'The offspring of this animal is an עולה, and the mother is a שלמים,' his words take effect. If he says, 'The mother is a שלמים, and her offspring is an עולה,' the offspring is the offspring of a שלמים. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with the order of someone's words when he consecrates a pregnant animal and its unborn offspring as two different קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he names the offspring first, it becomes an עולה before the mother is consecrated, so both of his statements work. If he names the mother first, the offspring already has her שלמים status, so his later words calling it an עולה cannot change it.

keyTerms.meaning: His words stand and take effect
The offspring of a שלמים, which has the status of a שלמים

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says: "The offspring of this animal is a burnt offering,
and the animal itself is a peace offering":
his words take effect.
If he says: "It is a peace offering, and its offspring is a burnt offering":
this is the offspring of a peace offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר ״וְלָדָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה, וְהִיא שְׁלָמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a related topic: consecrating a mother animal and its unborn offspring
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the words decides the outcome. If the mother is consecrated first, the offspring takes her status, according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: what he planned from the start counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר. If the person meant from the start to give the mother and the offspring different designations, both take effect. Only if he changed his mind afterward does the offspring stay a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: If that was his plan from the start, his words stand, since it is impossible to say two names at once. But if he said 'This is a שלמים' and only then changed his mind and said 'Its offspring is an עולה', the offspring is a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with רבי יוסי, who argues with רבי מאיר's ruling from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said that once the mother is called a שלמים, the offspring automatically becomes a שלמים. רבי יוסי says this happens only if the person truly changed his mind. If he planned both names from the beginning, the order of his words does not matter, because a person can only say one word at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Two designations at the same moment
His words stand (both designations take effect)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר looks at the order of the words. רבי יוסי looks at what the person intended from the start.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
If that is what he intended from the start,
since it is impossible
to call out two names at once,
his words stand;
but if, after he said 'This is a peace offering,'
he changed his mind and said 'Its offspring is a burnt offering,'
then its offspring is a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִם לְכֵן נִתְכַּוֵּין תְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view to רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he planned both designations from the start, both take effect. If he changed his mind only afterward, the offspring remains a שלמים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a pregnant חטאת and its offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי יוחנן. If someone sets aside a pregnant animal as a חטאת and it gives birth, he may get atonement with either the mother or the offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If someone set aside a pregnant animal as a חטאת and it gave birth, he may get atonement with the mother if he wants, or with the offspring if he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new rule from רבי יוחנן about a pregnant animal set aside as a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was already pregnant when it was set aside, so the הקדש covered both the mother and the fetus. Both therefore count as a חטאת, and the owner may choose which one to offer.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one set aside a pregnant animal as a sin offering and it gave birth,
if he wants, he gets atonement with the mother;
if he wants, he gets atonement with its offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הִפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת מְעוּבֶּרֶת וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion with a related rule about a pregnant animal that was set aside
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the mother and the offspring of a pregnant חטאת are usable, and the owner may choose either one.

steps.title: Asking for רבי יוחנן's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן rules this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's rule. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the fetus is just part of the mother, so it should not count as its own separate חטאת. The גמרא wants to know why it does.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why both the mother and the offspring count as usable חטאות

steps.title: A fetus is its own animal, like two חטאות set aside as backup
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that a fetus can be held back from the mother's הקדש, because a fetus is not just a part of its mother. So setting aside a pregnant חטאת is like setting aside two חטאות, one as a backup, and either one may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds that if a person holds back the fetus, it stays held back. A fetus is not just a limb of its mother. So it is like someone who sets aside two חטאות as a backup: he may get atonement with this one or with the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: according to רבי יוחנן, a fetus is a separate animal, so here there are really two חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that a person can choose to leave the fetus out of the mother's הקדש. That shows the fetus is its own animal and not a part of the mother's body. When both were sanctified together, it is just like setting aside two חטאות לאחריות, where the owner offers whichever one he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: If he held it back, it stays held back (the fetus can be left out of the הקדש)
A fetus is not considered a part of its mother's body
As a backup, in case one is lost

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי יוחנן's case, the owner did not hold back the fetus. The rule about holding it back is used only to show that the fetus is a separate animal, and that is why it gets its own holiness as a חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, עובר לאו ירך אמו: a pregnant animal set aside as a חטאת is like two separate חטאות, and the owner may choose either one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan holds:
if he held it back, it is held back.
phrases.notes: He means the fetus: if he sanctifies only the mother and leaves out the fetus, the fetus is not holy.

phrases.english: A fetus is not the thigh of its mother,
phrases.notes: 'Thigh' just means a body part. The fetus is not simply part of the mother's body.

phrases.english: so it is like one who sets aside
two sin offerings as a backup:
if he wants, he gets atonement with this one;
if he wants, he gets atonement with the other one.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִם שִׁיְּירוֹ מְשׁוּיָּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because רבי יוחנן holds עובר לאו ירך אמו, as shown by the rule that a fetus can be held back, the mother and the fetus are like two חטאות set aside as backup.

steps.title: The משנה calls it the offspring of a peace offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי יוחנן from the wording of our משנה. It says the offspring is 'the offspring of a שלמים', which sounds like its holiness comes from the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objected: The משנה says that if someone declares 'The mother is a שלמים and its offspring is an עולה,' the offspring is 'the offspring of a שלמים.' If a fetus can really be held back from the mother, the משנה should have said 'it is a שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks רבי יוחנן's idea that a fetus can be held back from the mother's הקדש. He points to the exact words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it the 'offspring of a שלמים' means its holiness is only borrowed from the mother. That fits the view that a fetus is just part of its mother. If the fetus had its own separate holiness, as רבי יוחנן says, the משנה should call it 'a שלמים' in its own right.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection (challenges a view from a source)
the offspring of a peace offering, holy only because of its mother
if he held it back, it stays held back (the fetus does not take the mother's status)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Offspring of a שלמים' and 'a שלמים' sound almost the same. The challenge depends on the difference: the first means borrowed holiness from the mother, and the second means holiness of its own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar raises an objection:
"It is a peace offering and its offspring is a burnt offering" —
it is the offspring of a peace offering.
And if it enters your mind
that if he held it back, it stays held back,
why does it say "it is the offspring of a peace offering"?
It should have taught "it is a peace offering"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given for רבי יוחנן in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a fetus can be held back from the mother's הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording, 'offspring of a שלמים', shows that the offspring's holiness comes from the mother. So the fetus is not separate from her.

steps.title: רב corrected the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב טבלא answers that this wording is not the correct one. רב told the reciter to say 'it is a שלמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טבלא said: Leave that version aside. רב told the תנא to recite it as 'it is a שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב טבלא answers רבי אלעזר's challenge by showing that the wording he relied on is not correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended entirely on the words 'offspring of a שלמים'. Once רב fixes the text to 'it is a שלמים', the משנה actually fits רבי יוחנן, because the offspring has holiness of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: leave that one aside (that version is not reliable)
a reciter who memorized and taught the משניות

phrases.english: Rav Tavla said:
Leave that one aside,
didn't Rav say to the reciter:
phrases.notes: The תנא here is the person in the study hall whose job was to memorize and recite משניות out loud.

phrases.english: Teach "it is a peace offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טַבְלָא בַּר מִינַּהּ דְּהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the text of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה reads 'offspring of a שלמים', which would mean the offspring's holiness comes from the mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is 'it is a שלמים', so the offspring has holiness of its own and there is no challenge to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The maidservant whose unborn child is freed
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge from a ברייתא: a master tells his pregnant שפחה that she stays a slave but her child is free, and the child does go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: If someone tells his שפחה, 'You are a maidservant, but your child is a free person,' and she was pregnant, she acquired freedom for the child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רבי יוחנן, this time from a ברייתא about freeing an unborn child. This step only presents the ruling, and the next step explains why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is like our offerings case: the mother keeps one status and the fetus is given a different one. The ruling is that the freedom works for the fetus. The גמרא is about to show which view of the fetus explains this.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew
she acquired it (freedom) on his behalf

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who says to his maidservant:
"You are a maidservant,
and your child is a free person,"
if she was pregnant
she acquired it for him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the unborn child, and 'it' is his freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 answered the first challenge, a second challenge to רבי יוחנן begins
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a fetus is not just a part of its mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling that frees the fetus while the mother stays a slave will be shown to depend on the fetus being part of the mother.

steps.title: This ruling fits the view that a fetus is part of its mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא makes sense if a fetus is part of its mother. Then freeing the fetus is like freeing half a slave, which works according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well if you say that holding back does not work and a fetus is like its mother's thigh. That is why she acquired freedom for the child: it is like someone who frees half of his slave. Whose view is that? רבי מאיר's, as a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the challenge. The ברייתא fits the view that a fetus is part of its mother, and that is the opposite of רבי יוחנן. The step ends by setting up a ברייתא of רבי מאיר, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fetus is a body part of the mother, freeing it means freeing part of the slave woman herself. That works, like freeing half a slave. The גמרא names רבי מאיר as the source of this ruling and gets ready to quote him. This suggests the ruling is harder to explain if the fetus is separate, as רבי יוחנן holds.

keyTerms.meaning: it works out well if you say
a fetus is like its mother's thigh, just a part of her body
one who frees half of his slave

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two sides. The ruling that the child goes free is explained here by the view that the fetus is PART of the mother, which is the opposite of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It works out well if you say
that if he held it back, it does not stay held back,
a fetus is the thigh of its mother,
phrases.notes: 'Thigh' is a picture for any body part. The fetus counts as a piece of the mother.

phrases.english: because of that she acquired freedom for him,
and it is like one who frees half of his slave.
And whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
as it is taught in a baraita:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אִם שִׁיְּירוֹ אֵינוֹ מְשׁוּיָּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic of the challenge brought in step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a fetus is separate from its mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's ruling is explained by the fetus being part of the mother, so it is like freeing half a slave according to רבי מאיר. This points against רבי יוחנן's view that the fetus is separate.
